claim: RULING 2 APPLIED. Section 1 paragraph 2 of OUTLINE.md no longer reports what the solver returned. It states that the located points are the COMPLETE solution set, proved by elimination, and it NAMES THE FIELD as Q(i sqrt 11). A drafting warning is attached in both section 1 and section 5 N1, because the error is attractive: the visible radicals in the solutions are sqrt 33, sqrt 11 and sqrt 3, which pulls a reader toward Q(sqrt 3, sqrt 11); the operator's commissioning ruling named that field, and this outline carried it until revision 4. The coefficients of the matching equations live in Q(i sqrt 11) via s_plus = -1/6 + i sqrt 11 / 6 and delta = -i sqrt 11 / 3, and sqrt 3 must NOT be adjoined, because it is generated by the eliminant. Adjoining it would split the two conjugate points and make a degree-2 ideal present as two degree-1 components for the wrong reason, destroying exactly the structure that the conjugacy statement reports.

The paragraph therefore credited the result to an argument the paper deliberately does NOT rest on. This matters beyond accuracy: the Odlyzko p. 77 page objects to Birkhoff-Trjitzinsky as possibly non-rigorous (S24-13), and section 2.0 is written to pre-empt that by stating nothing rests on it, so a method paragraph led by Pincherle invites precisely the question section 2.0 exists to close. FOUR THINGS TRAVEL WITH IT INTO SECTION 2, and the section-2 box is rewritten to carry all four. (i) The positivity hypothesis is LOAD-BEARING and must be stated rather than inherited from context: three of six sign-changing b violate the inequality outright, one of them because r_n becomes non-positive (S26-04). (ii) The upper half must NOT be written citing S1-02, which supplies the monotonicity step and the lower bound only; it carries S26-01. (iv) The insertion of the proposition into CT-S1-THEOREM/theorem.tex after prop:positive, about fifteen lines, is a DRAFTING ACTION AND IS NOT DONE: theorem.tex belongs to an earlier session and this corpus does not edit earlier sessions, so the LaTeX source of record still carries the one-sided statement only. The PREREG was left unedited and the correction written as a separate addendum.
